settings.heroSub: The students' association of the Faculty of Physical and Earth Sciences, University of Lagos. One faculty, six departments, two sub-departments, one voice.
settings.about:
PESSA is the students' association of the Faculty of Physical and Earth Sciences at the University of Lagos. It was founded in the 2025/2026 session to represent every student in the faculty and to run the programmes that shape student life: academics, sports, careers and social events.

The Pharonia is the second administration of PESSA, serving the 2026/2027 session. Our focus is to build systems that outlive us: a faculty that is united, fairly represented, and known for excellence in the classroom, on the field and in industry.

settings.presidentQuote:
The Faculty of Physical and Earth Sciences Students’ Association is driven by innovation, unity, and inclusivity. We are committed to promoting academic excellence, personal well-being, active sports participation, and meaningful relationships among our members.

news.title: Freshers' Orientation 2026 holds on 12 December
news.summary: New students of the faculty will be welcomed at Tayo Aderinokun Hall on Saturday, 12 December 2026, alongside the Freshers' Party and the Freshers' Cup.
news.body:
The Freshers' Orientation for the 2026/2027 session holds on Saturday, 12 December 2026 at Tayo Aderinokun Hall, University of Lagos.

Orientation is where new students meet the faculty, their departments and the PESSA executives. The Freshers' Party holds with the orientation, and the Freshers' Cup football tournament gives every department a team on the pitch.

Time, speakers and the full programme will be posted here and on Instagram @pessaunilag.

news.title: The Pharonia sets the vision for 2026/2027
news.summary: The second PESSA administration commits to a united and inclusive faculty that excels in academics, careers, sports and student life.
news.body:
Vision: A united and inclusive PESSA that excels academically, professionally, in sports and in student life, bridging the gap between the classroom and industry.

Mission: To build effective systems and programmes, from academic mentorship and industry networking to sports and social life, that drive excellence for every student, while ensuring fair representation and inclusion for all.

Unity, inclusion and fair representation sit at the heart of every programme this session.

news.title: Geosciences Center of Excellence
news.summary: The much-anticipated building for Geosciences lecture and Research was officially commissioned
news.body:
The University of Lagos (UNILAG) is set to host the commissioning of the Geosciences Centre of Excellence situated at its Science Complex (formerly the Faculty of Science) on Friday, April 17, 2026.

More than just a new building, the Centre represents a significant step forward in the University’s commitment to strengthening teaching, research, and real-world impact in the geosciences.

The project is the result of a strong collaboration, funded by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC), Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production Company Limited (SNEPCo), and the Nigeria Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB). Together, these partners have contributed to a legacy that will support not only today’s students and researchers, but generations to come.

Thoughtfully designed as a modern, three suspended-floor facility, the Centre brings together a range of spaces tailored for both learning and discovery. From laboratories and workshops to lecture theatres, a museum, simulation laboratory, and library, every part of the building has been created to encourage curiosity, collaboration, and hands-on experience. Offices, sit-out areas, and other support facilities complete a space that is as functional as it is forward-looking.

At its heart, the Geosciences Centre of Excellence reflects a simple but powerful idea: learning should not stop at theory. By strengthening the connection between the classroom and industry, the Centre creates opportunities for students and researchers to engage with real challenges and develop practical solutions that matter.

As the University prepares to unveil this new facility, it marks yet another moment in UNILAG’s continuing journey to grow, evolve, and contribute meaningfully to national and global development through knowledge and innovation.

news.title: Mathematics crowned overall champions of Dean's Games 2026
news.summary: The Department of Mathematics topped the Emergence '26 medal table with 10 gold medals and 59 points, ahead of Physics and Chemistry.
news.body:
The Dean's Games 2026, themed Emergence '26, came to an end on 19 June with the release of the official medal table.

Mathematics finished top with 10 gold, 8 silver and 3 bronze (59 points). Physics placed second with 33 points, Chemistry third with 32, followed by Geosciences (30), Statistics (22) and Environmental Standards (8).

Congratulations to every department. All athletes are advised to stay in competitive spirit ahead of the VC Games.

events.title: Freshers' Orientation 2026: The Blueprint for Success
events.description:
The 2025/2026 session's orientation welcomed freshers with two days of programming: a sports day and online orientation on 16 January, then the physical orientation and after-party on 17 January.

Sessions with industry leaders, academic and professional briefings, interaction with executives and senior colleagues, the Freshers' Novelty Match, music, giveaways and refreshments.

events.title: PESSA Innovation Challenge 2026 (PIC 2026)
events.description: The first-ever PESSA Innovation Challenge. Teams from all six departments picked a track, built a solution to a real Nigerian problem and pitched to industry judges on Demo Day, 27 June 2026, for a share of the ₦320,000 prize pool.

events.title: Dean's Games 2026: Emergence '26
events.description:
The faculty's inter-departmental games, 13 to 19 June 2026. Final medal table: Mathematics 59 points (10 gold), Physics 33, Chemistry 32, Geosciences 30, Statistics 22, Environmental Standards 8.

The Department of Mathematics were crowned overall champions and winners of the Dean's Cup.

faqs.q: Who is a member of PESSA?
faqs.a: Every student of the Faculty of Physical and Earth Sciences, University of Lagos, across its six departments and two sub-departments.

faqs.q: How do I reach the executives?
faqs.a: Call or WhatsApp the President or the General Secretary on the numbers on the Contact page, send an email to pessaunilag@gmail.com, or message @pessaunilag on Instagram.

faqs.q: How can an organisation partner with PESSA?
faqs.a: Visit the Partner With Us page to see our programmes and reach the executives directly.
